newsitem.title: UK: NWE FUEL OIL STEADY TO WEAKER BUT UNDERTONE STRONG.
newsitem.headline: NWE FUEL OIL STEADY TO WEAKER BUT UNDERTONE STRONG.

text.p: European fuel oil prices were steady to a little softer on Monday on the back of falling crude and swaps, but traders said high sulphur remained strong, supported basically by lack of prompt product.
"The undertone in the market is still strong, there's still a lack of physical barrels," a trader said.

Traders said high sulphur barges traded at $93.50, $94, $94.50, $94.75 and $95 a tonne fob ARA, compared with Friday's trade level of $94.50/$95. Some traders said some lower numbers were done by a trader for only 2,000 tonnes for pricing purposes while other deals simply reflected later loading dates.
Bunker demand was said to have improved late in the day, rising to more than 30,000 tonnes.
High sulphur fuel cargoes were steady to a shade weaker, with one cargo of high sulphur utility spec loading August 20 offered at $85 fob.
A cargo of 20-25,000 tonnes of high sulphur high density fuel was traded at $82 fob Le Havre.
Russian cracked cargoes continues to be offered at a steady two means +$1.5/$2 for better quality material and supplies were said to be on the low side.
